items.headline: Russia-Ukraine peace talks open in Abu Dhabi
items.summary: U.S.-mediated talks aimed at ending the war between Russia and Ukraine began in Abu Dhabi, with security guarantees for both sides on the agenda. The two countries exchanged strikes the day before the talks opened.

items.headline: Trump casts doubt on midterm results
items.summary: Trump questioned the honesty of the midterm elections in a social media post. He had earlier signaled that he accepted the results of the vote that gave Democrats control of Congress.

items.headline: Massie files articles to impeach Hegseth
items.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie filed a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and Trump said he would stand by him. Hegseth said he will hold a news conference to defend his decisions on Iran and Venezuela.

items.headline: Trump signals openness to immigration deal
items.summary: Trump said his deportation policy might have been too tough for midterm voters and that he could work with Democrats on immigration. Democrats are skeptical and want DACA and TPS protections restored first.

items.headline: China rejects Nvidia spy claims as company probes CEO
items.summary: Nvidia opened an investigation after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged a relationship with an executive U.S. intelligence reportedly tied to Beijing. China's government dismissed the spy allegations as a smear campaign.

items.headline: California voters reject billionaire tax
items.summary: California voters defeated Proposition 40, which would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on most billionaire wealth. The measure had divided Democrats.

items.headline: Senate advances permitting overhaul
items.summary: The Senate returned after the midterms and advanced a bipartisan bill to speed permitting reviews for data centers and other infrastructure. Environmental and Tribal groups say it favors gas-powered data centers.

items.headline: France blames Iran for supermarket fridge hack
items.summary: France said Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail sites, spoiling food. It called the attack sabotage.

items.headline: Fossil fuel emissions projected to fall in 2026
items.summary: Global Carbon Project research projects a 0.4% drop in fossil fuel emissions this year, driven by the Iran war energy shock and growth in wind and solar. China's emissions fell sharply last quarter amid the same energy disruptions.

items.headline: Trump's Israel aid cut is mostly a shift, experts say
items.summary: Trump said the U.S. is cutting aid to Israel. Experts say the change mainly moves the aid from the State Department to the Pentagon, with less congressional oversight.

digest.overview:
Trump questioned the honesty of the midterm elections in a social media post, days after signaling he accepted the results. He also said his deportation policy "might have been too tough" and floated an immigration deal; Democrats want DACA and TPS protections restored first. Rep. Thomas Massie filed a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, whom Trump said he stands by. The Senate returned for the lame-duck session and advanced a bipartisan permitting bill that critics say favors gas-powered data centers. California voters rejected Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on billionaire wealth. Trump said the FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman accused of spying for China, and Nvidia shares fell 4.27% on Monday.

Abroad, U.S.-mediated talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war began in Abu Dhabi, a day after the two sides traded strikes. France blamed Iranian military hackers for seizing refrigeration controls at about 700 retail sites and said it would seek European sanctions. China called the Nvidia spy allegations groundless. Experts said Trump's announced cut in aid to Israel mainly shifts the money from the State Department to the Pentagon. Novaya Gazeta, Russia's last major independent newspaper, is closing its office, citing government pressure. South Korean stocks rebounded after three straight losing sessions, and a government inspection found 354 suspected cases of fraudulent apartment subscriptions. A British court sentenced Russell Brand to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault. The Global Carbon Project projects fossil fuel emissions will fall 0.4% in 2026, partly due to the Iran war energy shock.

home.overview:
The Bills dominated Minnesota 23–6 on Monday night to move to 7-1, and the Vikings slipped behind the 7-2 Bears in the NFC North. Jacksonville loaded up before Tuesday's trade deadline, landing Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux, while Detroit added Andre Cisco. In the NBA, Cooper Flagg poured in 43 as Dallas edged Indiana 125–122, Victor Wembanyama had 40 points and 9 blocks in a rout at Phoenix, and the Lakers improved to 10-2 at Atlanta. Celtics at 76ers leads six games tonight, and Commanders at Giants opens Week 10 on Thursday. In baseball, Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart won Rookie of the Year.

Club soccer is on international break: the Nations League returns Thursday with England vs. Croatia and Italy vs. France, and Spain host England on Sunday. The Netherlands lost Virgil van Dijk, the USMNT called up Mark McKenzie for the injured George Campbell before Saturday's game against Haiti, and South Korea are in Doha for friendlies with Saudi Arabia and Qatar. Non-league Plymouth Parkway beat Berkhamsted 2–1 in extra time and will host Barnet in the FA Cup second round. K League 1 resumes Nov. 21 with Jeonbuk hosting champions FC Seoul. In the KBO offseason, champions Samsung turn to keeping free agents Koo Ja-wook and Won Tae-in.
